_comment: Facts that repeat across the site. Referenced from markup as {{phone.display}}.
Change a value here and every page that uses it changes on the next build —
that is the whole point: the annual price adjustment used to be 54 hand edits.
The build FAILS on an unknown placeholder, so a typo can never ship as literal
'{{...}}' text. Keep this file free of anything that is not a plain fact:
no markup, no copy, no per-page prose.

counters._comment: Cifras del Live-Entwurf. 300+/1.000.000+/10+ siguen SIN confirmar por el cliente (CLAUDE.md). 'count' es el valor crudo que lee el contador animado; el resto es como se muestra.

_comment: ALL PRICE NUMBERS ON THE SITE LIVE HERE (client rule G10, 2026-08-14: 'all price
values are adjusted once per year on our side — keep them editable in one place,
the update must be a 5-minute content edit'). Nothing below may be re-typed into
a page: every occurrence is a {{price.*}} token, so changing a number here changes
every page that states it, including the JSON-LD copies.
WHAT TO EDIT ONCE A YEAR:
min / max        the hourly range. `range` is the same pair joined with a hyphen
for the price box; keep all three in step.
surcharge.*      the collective-agreement percentages (Lohntarifvertrag Bayern).
example.*        the worked examples in the cost guide. These are DERIVED from
the rate, the hours and the surcharges — recompute them when the
rate moves, they do not update themselves.
guideYear        the year in the cost guide's <title> and og:title.
Source: the client's Webtexte. The RATE and the three worked examples come from
the 2026-08-17 pricing/positioning update (rev. 17.08.): 26-32 -> 24,50-32 net,
part of the shift to 'premium quality at the best price-performance ratio'. The
client fixed the glyph in the box as a SHORT HYPHEN (24,50-32), reconfirmed
2026-08-18 — their own update document writes an en dash, and they chose the
hyphen again, so do not 'correct' it. In BODY TEXT the range must read
'24,50 bis 32 Euro', which is why min/max exist next to range: a decimal comma
next to a hyphen (24,50-32 Euro) is ambiguous inside a sentence. Everything
else on this file is still Stand 04.08.2026.
RENAMED 2026-08-09 from 'werkschutz' to 'range': the Webtexte published the SAME
24,50-32 for every service and city, so a service-specific key invited a second,
drifting copy of one number. If a service ever gets its own range, add a key for
THAT service and leave this one as the default.
_floorComment: floor: the threshold in the cost guide's 'Warum billig teuer wird' section
('Stundensätze deutlich unter 24 Euro'). It is NOT price.min and must not be
replaced by it: the client deliberately names a rounder number just below the
range, so the sentence reads as an industry floor rather than as FRANKONIA's
own bottom rate. Before 2026-08-17 the page did use min, which worked while
min was a whole 26 and reads wrong as 'deutlich unter 24,50 Euro'.

_comment: The cost guide's three worked examples. REWRITTEN 2026-08-17 (Webtext 32,
rev. 13.08./17.08.): each example now derives its surcharges in the open
instead of stating a total, so every intermediate figure is a value of its
own here. That was not cosmetic — with the 24,50 rate and the OLD wording the
page printed '72 x 24,50-32 = grob 1.950-2.500' while that multiplication
gives 1.764-2.304, because the client's new totals have the surcharges baked
in and the sentence still said they came on top. A visible sum that does not
compute. Keep base + surcharge + total in step: total = base + surcharges.

_priceBoxComment: Defaults for partials/price-box.html, added 2026-08-16 for the nine service
pages. Same mechanism and same reason as nameRequired/companyRequired below:
an include's own parameters WIN over this file, so a page overrides one line
by passing e.g. priceBoxTick1="Kurzfristig verfügbar nach Absprache" and every
other page keeps the default without being edited. They live at the TOP LEVEL
because an include parameter is a flat key and cannot override a nested one.
Why they exist: each Webtext specifies its own Preis-Box lines, and /brandwache/
specifies a PHONE CTA there rather than the form (its whole page inverts the CTA
order — client rule G2, the one approved exception). Before this the box was
fixed, so those lines were the one part of a draft the price section could not
state. Nothing about the 11 pages that already include the box changed.

_ogimageComment: The social-share image (og:image + twitter:image), emitted for EVERY page by
partials/head-common.html. This value is the FALLBACK: the homepage hero.
Why it is here and not in each page: all 54 pages declared
twitter:card="summary_large_image" while only the homepage declared an
og:image at all, and that file had never been created - so every link shared
to WhatsApp, LinkedIn or Slack rendered as a bare text row with no picture.
THE RULE (client, 2026-08-21): a page uses its OWN hero photograph; a page
with no hero photograph falls back to the homepage hero. The 15 pages that
have one override this by passing the parameter on their own include:
The other 39 pass nothing and get this value. Top level, like nameRequired:
an include parameter is a flat key and cannot override a nested one.
The files are 1200x630 JPEGs generated once from the hero photos by
docs/design-sources/og-images.ps1 - see that script for why they are cropped
copies rather than the hero files themselves (nine heroes are portrait, and a
portrait og:image gets centre-cropped into a landscape card by every
platform). Re-run it after replacing a hero photo.
_formComment: nameRequired/companyRequired: banderas del partial lead-form. Por defecto ambos obligatorios; una página las sobrescribe en su include, p.ej. nameRequired="" para bajar la fricción en una landing de Ads. Van al nivel superior porque un parámetro de include es una clave plana y no puede sobrescribir una anidada.
